text: You're a fool, Mr. Velichkov! Look, I like you so much. Why should we deceive the younger generation, let's reveal our cards. Ideals! Boschlaf! Our personal earthly contentment - that's the ideal we should pursue. I'm glad you've already achieved this truth. And does this vile people deserve to be feared for? When we were younger, it was all right; but now - we've become forty-somethings, we should think about ourselves. What a waste! And you, you wretch, you tortured yourself through these Istanbul alleys, through these Italian... wasn't that quite a feat? When you saw that Stambolov was furious, you took your pears from Bulgaria, abandoned these slaves, let them swim in slavery. They're trained. You haven't been trained to pull and, like any gentleman, you tried to dodge. What's bothering you in this empty Halki - and sometimes you didn't have enough money for doctors. Bobchev and Madzharov fell silent. Enough of the exploits. Well, you know what - take it, and throw away your empty poetry. That's fine, but when the wind blows in the pocket, and now, thank God, we've got it sorted out. Now they'll start, all sorts of kids, all sorts of socialists, idealists, to bark at you, but don't blink an eye! Make yourself deaf, and look after yourself, and both look after yourself and laugh at their intelligence. You know what. Why would they bark at you? A wink at some betrayal of yours, a deception, out of disappointment? Oh! Out of envy? Of course! Without a doubt! Without a doubt out of envy! And why? Simply because their bones were crushed, their throats were shaking, and you (you're a terrible devil, may the darkness take you!) just shook yourself ready to the warmest place. Well, do you see now! Candace? Didn't I tell you that the best thing in this world is to be warm? This social struggle, ideals and I don't know what nonsense - it's all bullshit! Now, when you put your bag on the end of the month, that when fifteen hundred left-handed people come at you... A good thing, damn it! Hold on now! If you've got your hands on the bone - hold on! Don't even think about whose skin these left-handed people are being torn from... Pound the flour sack, his old mother! Pound! He's letting out...

But you may wonder why I am writing you this letter. I am writing it to praise you for your speech in the National Assembly the other day. Well done, Kocho! Well, to tell you the truth, I burst into tears of joy. I was about to come to you and kiss you in front of all the deputies. But they will start stamping their feet, objecting... Do you remember which speech? How could you not remember? The whole world is talking about it. But you are right, Kocho! It is not possible for so many thousands of voters to tear apart twenty gendarmes and a fifty-man drunken gang. A big deal! The gendarmes would have shot a hundred voters at most! Well, is it a big deal? All in all, about two hundred houses would have been burned down. Let's say, the army will come next Sunday and shoot, kill at most, three hundred people at most. How many orphaned houses - five hundred houses! Happy, they are talking!...

Well, they, the couch potatoes, have started to tame the crowd, not a hair falls out! How can you not be indignant?... Thanks to such soft couch potatoes, you have been waiting in Halki for eight whole years... To write them so many poems about the stars and sighs, and they make you wait for eight years. Eight years! Shame on the Bulgarian people. If at least a hundred thousand voters from all over Bulgaria had gone under the bullets, you could have taken your warm place today much earlier. But you scoundrels! Cowards! What is this lawfulness and freedom for, if at least a thousand voters are not exterminated?... Hold on, dear Kocho, I like you so much. Give such speeches more often, to inspire greater confidence in the great gates... so watch your own heart! That the younger generation would be indignant, that the people would be excited - don't even blink an eye! The people! The people are a herd when you swing a club at them... So, finally, am I going to teach you these things?!...

I am most glad that it was you who rushed to give this speech, no one could beat you to it. Artak, if you haven't inspired them with confidence even now, where will you be more so!... All the chorbajis praise you! We are affluent, they say, Kocho has become our man, he has finally come to his senses. Now, get your wits about you, hold on this time, and don't be afraid!... But keep an eye on it, Kocho, put some money aside, you never know - you're as bright as a flower!

Kocho, when you read this letter - grab it, so that it doesn't fall into the hands of the guy who described me traveling around Europe, so that he can print me out somewhere again. I heard him the other day, he was saying to someone: "Wow, you idiot, I didn't expect those words from our Velichkov"... - so I listen to him and wonder about his mind. The wind is blowing... Kocho, why are you still publishing this empty "Progress"? Dump him! Aslı and his name is such a kid, he doesn't look like a solid man like you anymore. So if you're so itching to write - write, but it would be most appropriate to call the newspaper "It's Not His Time" and then our partisans would call themselves non-Jewish.
I brought a few muskets in my saddlebags. Can't you make up some law to spray public buildings with gun oil?
